name: alpha-brackets-web

scripts.//perf: Production Lighthouse. Always use this rather than pointing Lighthouse at `next dev`: a dev build ships a ~213 KB devtools chunk, the HMR client and unminified JS, which inflates simulated LCP by seconds. See scripts/perf.mjs.

//browserslist: Matches Tailwind v4's own floor (Chrome 111, Safari 16.4, Firefox 128), which this project already depends on for @property, color-mix and cascade layers, so the CSS could not render on anything older anyway. Added in response to a Lighthouse 'Legacy JavaScript, 8 KiB' finding, but it saved nothing: production builds with and without this key are byte-identical. Two corrections to an earlier version of this note, both found by measuring. (1) A polyfill chunk IS emitted, about 110 KB; an earlier check missed it because the chunk is hash-named and the grep looked for 'poly' in filenames. (2) It does not matter, because the built HTML loads it as `<script noModule>`, so no browser that supports ES modules ever downloads it. The Lighthouse finding itself came from a dev-only chunk. Keep this key because it pins the target and documents the floor, not because it saved bytes.
